user.title: Australian Emergency Services
user.description: Configure emergency incident tracking for your state or territory.

data_description.states: Select which Australian states to monitor for emergency incidents
data_description.state: Select which Australian state to monitor for emergency incidents
data_description.update_interval: How often to poll for new incidents, in seconds (60 to 86400, default 600)
data_description.remove_stale: Remove incident entities when they are no longer active, instead of marking them unavailable
data_description.expose_to_assistants: Expose newly created incident entities to Assist and Google Assistant
data_description.zones: Select Home Assistant zones to filter incidents. Incidents will show which zones they fall within.
data_description.radius: Only create map entities for incidents within this distance of home. 0 keeps every incident in the selected states. Sensors always count the whole state.
data_description.alert_radius: The Emergency nearby sensor turns on for incidents within this distance of home, or when home is inside a warning area.
data_description.alert_min_severity: Lowest severity that turns the Emergency nearby sensor on. ACT incidents carry no warning level and only count at Info.
data_description.zone_buffer: Distance added to each monitored zone's own radius when deciding whether an incident is in that zone.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Australian Emergency Services is already configured. Use its options to change the monitored states.

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Forces an immediate refresh of all incident data from the source.

remove_state.name: Remove State
remove_state.description: Removes the device and all entities for a specific state. Use this to clean up orphaned devices.

state.name: State
state.description: The state code to remove (SA, NSW, VIC, QLD, TAS, WA or ACT).

feed_unavailable.title: {state} emergency feed is unavailable
feed_unavailable.description:
The {state} incident feed has failed {failures} updates in a row, so its sensors and map entities are unavailable. Treat this as unknown, not as no incidents, and check your state's emergency website directly. The integration keeps retrying and clears this message when the feed recovers.

Last error: {error}

sa_map_fallback.title: SA incidents are using the CFS map fallback
sa_map_fallback.description: The SA CRIIMSON feed is unavailable, so SA incidents come from the public CFS map layer. That layer can include old records and does not provide CAP warnings. Do not rely on it as an all clear. This message clears when CRIIMSON recovers.

state_without_feed.title: {state} has no incident feed
state_without_feed.description: {state} no longer publishes a machine-readable incident feed, so its sensors stay unavailable. Remove {state} in the integration's options to stop this message.
